title: Overlapping Schwarz and stable subspace decompositions

items.title: Elementwise P1 product-cutoff energy estimate
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $d\ge2$ and let $K$ be a nondegenerate affine
$d$-simplex in a shape-regular mesh with $h_K/\rho_K\le\sigma$. Let
$\theta,w\in\mathbb P_1(K)$. Let $I_K(\theta w)\in\mathbb P_1(K)$ be the affine
function whose values at the vertices of $K$ are the nodal values of
$\theta w$. There is a constant $C$ depending only on $d$ and the shape
regularity bound $\sigma$ such that
$$ \|\nabla I_K(\theta w)\|_{L^2(K)} \le C\bigl(\|\theta\nabla w\|_{L^2(K)} +\|w\nabla\theta\|_{L^2(K)}\bigr). $$
items.strategy: Use vertex differences of the affine nodal product, affine scaling of barycentric gradients, and finite-dimensional L2 control of P1 nodal values.

items.title: Finite-dimensional Schwarz subspace-correction data
items.statement:
Work in exact real arithmetic. Let $n\ge1$ and $V=\mathbb R^n$, and let
$A=A^{\mathsf T}$ satisfy $x^{\mathsf T}Ax>0$ for every nonzero $x$.
Give $V$ the energy inner product $a(x,y)=x^{\mathsf T}Ay$ and norm
$\|x\|_A^2=a(x,x)$ of
[[def-energy-inner-product-and-norm-for-a-hermitian-positive-definite-matrix]].
An operator $S$ is $A$-self-adjoint when $a(Sx,y)=a(x,Sy)$ for all $x,y$;
it is positive when $a(Sx,x)>0$ for every nonzero $x$. An $A$-orthogonal
projection is an idempotent $A$-self-adjoint operator.
Let $\mathcal I$ be a finite ordered nonempty set and, for each
$i\in\mathcal I$, choose a full-column-rank prolongation
$R_i\in\mathbb R^{n\times n_i}$ with $1\le n_i\le n$, and put
$V_i=\operatorname{Ran}(R_i)$.
A one-level method has $\mathcal I=\{1,\ldots,m\}$. A two-level method has
$\mathcal I=\{0,1,\ldots,m\}$, where $R_0=P$ and $V_0$ is the designated
coarse space. Restriction of a global residual is $R_i^{\mathsf T}$ and
prolongation of a local coefficient vector is $R_i$. Define the local energy
matrix
$$A_i=R_i^{\mathsf T}AR_i.$$
When the coarse index $0$ is present, $A_0=P^{\mathsf T}AP$ is the Galerkin
coarse matrix of [[def-galerkin-coarse-grid-correction]]. By
[[thm-galerkin-coarse-correction-is-energy-orthogonal-projector]], it is SPD
and the exact coarse solve is well-defined.

For each $i\in\mathcal I$, the exact local correction and additive
preconditioner are
$$ \Pi_i=R_iA_i^{-1}R_i^{\mathsf T}A, \qquad B=\sum_{i\in\mathcal I}R_iA_i^{-1}R_i^{\mathsf T}. $$
When the spaces span $V$, the exact additive Schwarz preconditioned operator
is $BA=\sum_{i\in\mathcal I}\Pi_i$. For a fixed ordering of $\mathcal I$, a
multiplicative sweep applies its corrections in that order; if $0$ is present,
it is first. For an inexact additive method, replace each exact $A_i^{-1}$ by
the inverse of an SPD matrix $\widetilde A_i$ satisfying, for fixed
$0<\alpha\le\beta$,
$$ \alpha A_i\preceq \widetilde A_i\preceq\beta A_i, \qquad \widetilde B=\sum_{i\in\mathcal I}R_i\widetilde A_i^{-1}R_i^{\mathsf T}. $$
For symmetric matrices, $X\preceq Y$ means
$z^{\mathsf T}Xz\le z^{\mathsf T}Yz$ for every vector $z$. The order
inequalities define uniform local spectral equivalence in this pair. The
lemma [[lem-schwarz-local-matrices-are-well-defined]] proves the remaining
local inverse and well-definedness claims.
items.strategy: Specify global and local spaces, restrictions/prolongations, exact and inexact local solves, the coarse space, and the additive and multiplicative operators in exact arithmetic.

items.title: Schwarz local matrices and exact solves are well defined
items.statement:
For the data of [[def-overlapping-schwarz-subspace-correction-data]], every
local matrix $A_i=R_i^{\mathsf T}AR_i$ with $i\in\mathcal I$ is symmetric
positive definite and therefore invertible. If the coarse index $0$ is
present, then $A_0=P^{\mathsf T}AP$ is the SPD Galerkin coarse matrix. Hence
every exact local solve in the definition exists uniquely.
items.strategy: Use the actual Galerkin coarse-projector supplier for i=0 and injectivity with the global energy for the remaining local matrices.

items.title: Stable two-level P1 decomposition for structured Poisson meshes
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $d\in\{2,3\}$, $\Omega=(0,1)^d$, and let
$M\ge2$ and $n\ge2$ be integers. Write $e_1,\ldots,e_d$ for the standard
coordinate vectors in $\mathbb R^d$. In every cube of side $a=1/M$, for each
coordinate permutation $\pi$ use the simplex whose successive vertices,
with $x$ the cube's lower corner, are
$x$, $x+a e_{\pi(1)}$, $x+a(e_{\pi(1)}+e_{\pi(2)})$, through
$x+a\sum_{r=1}^d e_{\pi(r)}$. Subdivide each cube into $n^d$ uniform fine
cubes and apply the same permutation rule at fine scale; this gives a
matching, shape-regular affine simplicial fine mesh refining the coarse mesh.
Write $H=\sqrt d\,a$ and
$h=\sqrt d\,a/n$. Assume an overlap radius $\delta=q a/n$ with integer
$\lceil\sqrt d\rceil\le q\le n$, so $h\le\delta\le a$. For each
coarse cube $Q_j$, let $\Omega_j$ be its closed $\ell^\infty$-neighborhood of
radius $\delta+h$, intersected with $\overline\Omega$. Let $V_H\subset V_h
\subset H_0^1(\Omega)$ be the continuous zero-boundary P1 spaces on the
coarse and fine meshes, and let
$$ V_j=\{v_h\in V_h:\operatorname{supp}v_h\subseteq\Omega_j\}. $$
Here $\|x\|_\infty=\max_r|x_r|$,
$\operatorname{dist}_\infty(x,Q)=\inf_{y\in Q}\|x-y\|_\infty$, an
$\ell^\infty$-neighborhood of radius $r$ is
$\{x:\operatorname{dist}_\infty(x,Q)\le r\}$, and $\operatorname{supp}v$ is
the closure in $\overline\Omega$ of $\{x:v(x)\ne0\}$.
For the Poisson energy $a(u,v)=\int_\Omega\nabla u\cdot\nabla v\,dx$, every
$u_h\in V_h$ has a decomposition $u_h=u_0+\sum_j u_j$ with
$u_0\in V_H$ and $u_j\in V_j$ satisfying
$$ a(u_0,u_0)+\sum_j a(u_j,u_j) \le C_{\rm FE}\left(1+\left(\frac H\delta\right)^2\right)a(u_h,u_h). $$
The constant $C_{\rm FE}$ depends only on $d$, the fixed uniform
shape-regularity bound, the Scott–Zhang constant, and the reference P1 product
interpolation constants; it is independent of $M,n,\delta$.
items.strategy: Apply the boundary-preserving Scott-Zhang coarse map, construct a nonnegative bounded-overlap partition of unity with gradient O(delta^{-1}), interpolate each cutoff times the coarse residual, and sum the local energy bounds.

items.title: Exact Schwarz local corrections are energy-orthogonal projections
items.statement:
For the data of [[def-overlapping-schwarz-subspace-correction-data]], every
$\Pi_i=R_iA_i^{-1}R_i^{\mathsf T}A$ is an $A$-orthogonal projection, meaning
an idempotent $A$-self-adjoint operator, with range $V_i$. Consequently, for every
$x\in V$,
$$ \|x\|_A^2=\|\Pi_i x\|_A^2+\|(I-\Pi_i)x\|_A^2, \qquad a(\Pi_i x,x)=\|\Pi_i x\|_A^2. $$
items.strategy: Multiply the local restriction/prolongation formula and use the Galerkin supplier for the coarse space.

items.title: The additive Schwarz inverse minimizes summed local energy
items.statement:
For the data of [[def-overlapping-schwarz-subspace-correction-data]], assume
$\sum_{i\in\mathcal I}V_i=V$. Let
$R=[R_i]_{i\in\mathcal I}$ and
$\mathcal D=\operatorname{diag}(A_i)_{i\in\mathcal I}$, so
$B=R\mathcal D^{-1}R^{\mathsf T}$. Then $B$ is SPD and, for every $x\in V$,
$$ x^{\mathsf T}B^{-1}x = \min_{\substack{z=(z_i)_{i\in\mathcal I}\\Rz=x}} \sum_{i\in\mathcal I}z_i^{\mathsf T}A_i z_i. $$
items.strategy: Assemble the local matrices block-diagonally, construct the unique feasible minimizer from B^{-1}x, and prove every other feasible vector adds a nonnegative nullspace energy.

items.title: Additive Schwarz condition bound from stable decomposition and synthesis
items.statement:
Use the data of [[def-overlapping-schwarz-subspace-correction-data]] and
assume the local spaces span $V$. Suppose $0<C_0,C_1<\infty$ satisfy:

- for every $x\in V$, there are local vectors $z_i$ such that
  $x=\sum_iR_i z_i$ and $\sum_i z_i^{\mathsf T}A_i z_i\le C_0\|x\|_A^2$;
- for every tuple $(z_i)$,
  $\|\sum_iR_i z_i\|_A^2\le C_1\sum_i z_i^{\mathsf T}A_i z_i$.

For an $A$-self-adjoint positive operator $T$, define
$$ \lambda_{\min}^A(T)=\inf_{x\ne0}\frac{a(Tx,x)}{a(x,x)},\qquad \lambda_{\max}^A(T)=\sup_{x\ne0}\frac{a(Tx,x)}{a(x,x)},\qquad \kappa_A(T)=\frac{\lambda_{\max}^A(T)}{\lambda_{\min}^A(T)}. $$
Then the exact additive Schwarz operator $T=BA$ is $A$-self-adjoint positive and
$$ \lambda_{\min}^A(BA)\ge C_0^{-1},\qquad \lambda_{\max}^A(BA)\le C_1,\qquad \kappa_A(BA)\le C_0C_1. $$
If the inexact local matrices satisfy
$\alpha A_i\preceq\widetilde A_i\preceq\beta A_i$ for
$0<\alpha\le\beta$, then
$$ \lambda_{\min}^A(\widetilde BA)\ge(\beta C_0)^{-1},\qquad \lambda_{\max}^A(\widetilde BA)\le C_1/\alpha,\qquad \kappa_A(\widetilde BA)\le(\beta/\alpha)C_0C_1. $$
items.strategy: Use the energy projection identity for the lower Rayleigh bound, the synthesis inequality for the upper bound, and variational inverse comparison for uniformly spectrally equivalent local solvers.

items.title: Multiplicative Schwarz projection sweeps contract with explicit overlap constants
items.statement:
Use the exact data of
[[def-overlapping-schwarz-subspace-correction-data]], with one coarse space
$V_0$ and $m\ge1$ local spaces $V_1,\ldots,V_m$. Assume the stable-decomposition
and synthesis hypotheses of
[[thm-additive-schwarz-stable-decomposition-condition-number]] hold with
constants $C_0,C_1$. Suppose a symmetric matrix
$G=(\epsilon_{ij})_{i,j=1}^m$ has nonnegative entries and
$$ |a(v_i,v_j)|\le\epsilon_{ij}\|v_i\|_A\|v_j\|_A \quad(v_i\in V_i,\ v_j\in V_j). $$
For a real matrix $M$, write $\|M\|_2=\sup_{y\ne0}\|My\|_2/\|y\|_2$ for its
induced Euclidean operator norm. Set $\rho=\|G\|_2$ and
$K=1+2C_1+2(1+\rho)^2$. For the coarse-first exact multiplicative sweep
$E_{\mathrm{mult}}=(I-\Pi_m)\cdots(I-\Pi_1)(I-\Pi_0)$,
$$ \|E_{\mathrm{mult}}\|_A^2 \le 1-\frac{1}{C_0K}<1. $$
The ordered factors need not commute. Here
$\|S\|_A=\sup_{x\ne0}\|Sx\|_A/\|x\|_A$ is the induced operator norm.
items.strategy: Telescope exact energy decreases, compare additive projection energies to sweep corrections using the overlap matrix, and apply the stable lower Rayleigh bound.

items.title: Two-level overlapping P1 Poisson bounds with explicit H-overlap dependence
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. For the two-level P1 Poisson family of
[[thm-two-level-p1-poisson-stable-decomposition]], let
$N_0=7^d$ and $N_1=11^d$. The coarse-plus-local synthesis constant can be
chosen as $C_1=1+N_0$, and the local overlap matrix can be chosen with
$\rho\le N_1$. Consequently, for the exact additive Schwarz operator,
$$ \kappa_A(BA)\le C_{\rm FE}\left(1+(H/\delta)^2\right)(1+7^d). $$
For the coarse-first exact multiplicative sweep,
$$ \|E_{\rm mult}\|_A^2\le 1-\frac{1}{ C_{\rm FE}(1+(H/\delta)^2) \left(1+2(1+7^d)+2(1+11^d)^2\right) }<1. $$
In particular, if $H/\delta$ is uniformly bounded, both estimates are
independent of the fine mesh size and the number of subdomains. These are
constant-coefficient Poisson bounds; they assert no robustness for arbitrary
coefficient contrast or anisotropy.
items.strategy: Count local supports per element and neighboring padded cubes, then substitute the resulting constants into the abstract additive and multiplicative theorems.

title: Overlapping Schwarz and stable subspace decompositions — Examples

items.title: The stable-splitting guarantee worsens as overlap shrinks
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. For any admissible overlap radius $\delta$ in the
structured family of
[[thm-two-level-p1-poisson-stable-decomposition]], put $r=H/\delta$.
Substitution into the proved stable-decomposition guarantee gives
$$ C_0\le C_{\rm FE}(1+r^2). $$
Along admissible families with $\delta/H\to0$, this upper-bound formula grows.
This substitution does not assert that the actual stable constant or
condition number must diverge.
items.strategy: Substitute r=H/delta into the established one-sided bound and keep the implication direction explicit.

items.title: One-level point-patch Schwarz loses uniformity on 1D Poisson
items.statement:
For the uniform $N$-interval P1 discretization of the Dirichlet Poisson problem
on $(0,1)$, one-level exact point-patch additive Schwarz has
$$ \kappa_A(BA)=\frac{1+\cos(\pi/N)}{1-\cos(\pi/N)}. $$
The patches are the supports of the interior nodal hats; they overlap with
their neighbors and have bounded multiplicity. Nevertheless the condition
number diverges with the number $N-1$ of local spaces.
items.strategy: Diagonalize the Dirichlet tridiagonal stiffness matrix with its sine vectors and compute the exact local point-patch preconditioner.

items.title: A one-node coarse space misses a high-conductance channel
items.statement:
A bounded-size one-node coarse space, together with bounded-overlap exact
local solves, guarantees an additive Schwarz condition number uniform in every
positive diffusion contrast.
items.strategy: Give the two-by-two SPD graph diffusion matrix, compute its local solves and eigenvalues, and let alpha grow.

items.title: A uniform two-level 1D Poisson correction bound
items.statement:
Let $N=2M$ with $M\ge2$ on the uniform fine P1 Dirichlet mesh of $(0,1)$.
Take the coarse P1 space on the even nodes and one local space
$\operatorname{span}\{\phi_{2k-1}\}$ for each odd node. The exact two-level
additive Schwarz operator has $C_0\le2$, $C_1\le2$, and hence
$\kappa_A(BA)\le4$, independently of $M$.
items.strategy: Decompose each fine nodal vector into its even-node linear interpolant and odd-node residuals, then compare each energy exactly interval by interval.

items.title: Inexact local solves enter through spectral-equivalence constants
items.statement:
Take $A=I_2$ and the two coordinate subspaces. Exact local matrices are
$A_1=A_2=1$, so the exact preconditioner is $B=I_2$ and its condition number
is $1$. Choose inexact local matrices
$\widetilde A_1=4$ and $\widetilde A_2=1/2$. They satisfy
$\frac14 A_i\preceq\widetilde A_i\preceq4A_i$, while
$\widetilde B=\operatorname{diag}(1/4,2)$ and
$\kappa_A(\widetilde BA)=8$. The theorem's bound is
$(\beta/\alpha)C_0C_1=16$.
items.strategy: Compute the exact diagonal additive preconditioner, its eigenvalues, and the uniform local spectral-equivalence interval.
